- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early in horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., >85.0) after a spike — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for such events.  
- Model overestimates downward moves in early horizon when sentiment is neutral — cap forecast decline at 1–2% below recent low.  
- Forecast shows gradual upward drift but true outcome often reverses mid-horizon — introduce early mean-reversion bias (e.g., reduce slope after 10–15 days).  
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture peak — add 1–2% buffer to forecast at 15–20 day mark.  
- When sentiment history includes 0.33 or higher, model tends to over-forecast — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.
